title: Artin Presentation Completeness and Braid Combing

items.title: The Zariski combing words α_i and x_i in the Artin presentation
items.statement: Fix n≥2 and let B_n=⟨σ_1,…,σ_{n−1}⟩ be the abstract braid group of [[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]], with words read first letter first and first-under-second stacking. For 1≤i≤n−1 put α_i:=σ_iσ_{i+1}⋯σ_{n−1}∈B_n, and put α_n:=1. For 1≤i≤n−1 put x_i:=σ_{n−1}^{−1}⋯σ_{i+1}^{−1}σ_i²σ_{i+1}⋯σ_{n−1}=α_{i+1}^{−1}σ_i²α_{i+1}. The two displayed words for x_i are equal by free cancellation, so x_i is unambiguous. These are the Zariski combing words; the definition is choice-free, uses no relation of the presentation, and asserts no property of these elements in any geometric model.
items.proof_strategy: Read every product in the fixed letter order and record the free cancellation α_{i+1}^{−1}σ_i²α_{i+1}=σ_{n−1}^{−1}⋯σ_{i+1}^{−1}σ_i²σ_{i+1}⋯σ_{n−1} of the two expanded words; both sides are words in the given generators and their inverses, so no defining relation is used. Keep α_n=1 as the empty word and note x_{n−1}=σ_{n−1}². Because the definition makes no geometric claim, it can be stated before any geometric braid construction is used, and all later items may substitute either displayed form of x_i at will.

items.title: Prefix insertion rewrites a trivial braid word into combing factors
items.statement: Assume n≥2. Let W=σ_{i₁}^{ε₁}⋯σ_{i_m}^{ε_m} have trivial image under the published surjection φ to geometric braids. For each prefix W_k put j_k=π(φ(W_k))^{-1}(n), the position reached by following the tracked point top-to-bottom through the first k letters. Then j₀=j_m=n and j_k=s_{i_k}(j_{k−1}). Using only free insertion of α_jα_j^{-1}, W≡∏_{k=1}^m(α_{j_{k−1}}^{-1}σ_{i_k}^{ε_k}α_{j_k}). Read bottom-to-top, the tracked point starts at n below each factor, reaches j_k below its letter, leaves the letter at j_{k−1} above it, and returns to n.
items.proof_strategy: Define j_k from the inverse endpoint permutation of each prefix; because the first letter is the top layer, the inverse permutation follows the tracked point top-to-bottom and gives j_k=s_{i_k}(j_{k−1}). The trivial endpoint permutation gives j₀=j_m=n. Insert α_{j_k}α_{j_k}^{−1} between consecutive letters; with α_n=1 the factors telescope to W by free cancellation only. For each factor, read its layers bottom-to-top: α_{j_k} takes n to the below position j_k, the letter takes it to the above position j_{k−1}, and α_{j_{k−1}}^{-1} returns it to n. This agrees with the six-case item’s below/above convention.

items.title: Each combing factor reduces to a lower-rank letter or an x-letter
items.statement: Assume n≥2 and use the words of [[def-zariski-braid-combing-words-alpha-and-x]]. Let 1≤j≤n be a position, 1≤k≤n−1 an index and ε∈{±1}, and let the combing factor be F=α_j^{−1}σ_k^{ε}α_{j′}, where j′=k+1 if j=k, j′=k if j=k+1, and j′=j otherwise; in the bottom-to-top reading of F, j′ is the position below the letter and j is the position above it, with j′=s_k(j). Using only the two Artin relations and free cancellations and insertions: F reduces to the empty word if j=k and ε=1; to x_k^{−1} if j=k and ε=−1; to x_k if j=k+1 and ε=1; to the empty word if j=k+1 and ε=−1; to σ_k^{ε} if k<j−1; and to σ_{k−1}^{ε} if k>j. In every case the reduced form involves only σ_1,…,σ_{n−2}, x_1,…,x_{n−1} and their inverses.
items.proof_strategy: Use j′=s_k(j), with j′ below the letter and j above it in the bottom-to-top reading. When j=k or j=k+1, substitute α_k=σ_kα_{k+1} and x_k=α_{k+1}^{−1}σ_k²α_{k+1} to obtain the four cancellation/x cases. If k<j−1, every index in α_j is at least k+2, so far commutation reduces F to σ_k^ε. If k>j, write α_j=(σ_j⋯σ_{k−2})σ_{k−1}σ_k(σ_{k+1}⋯σ_{n−1}); commute the distant factors and apply the three-strand relation to get σ_k^εα_j≡α_jσ_{k−1}^ε, hence F≡σ_{k−1}^ε. The index bounds put all surviving letters in σ_1,…,σ_{n−2}. Apply the published geometric relation suppliers to transfer the same identities to geometric braids.

items.title: Lower-rank Artin letters conjugate x-letters
items.statement: Assume n≥3, and let 1≤i≤n−2 and 1≤j≤n−1. With the words of [[def-zariski-braid-combing-words-alpha-and-x]] and using only the two Artin relations and free cancellations: σ_i^{−1}x_jσ_i equals x_j when j<i or j>i+1, equals x_{i+1}x_ix_{i+1}^{−1} when j=i+1, and equals x_{i+1} when j=i; and σ_ix_jσ_i^{−1} equals x_j when j<i or j>i+1, equals x_i when j=i+1, and equals x_i^{−1}x_{i+1}x_i when j=i. Consequently, in any word in σ_1^{±1},…,σ_{n−2}^{±1},x_1^{±1},…,x_{n−1}^{±1} each occurrence of a lower-rank σ-letter can be moved to the right of every x-letter, changing the x-letters only by further x-letters and their inverses.
items.proof_strategy: Expand x_j=σ_{n−1}^{−1}⋯σ_{j+1}^{−1}σ_j²σ_{j+1}⋯σ_{n−1}. For j<i or j>i+1, all relevant generators far-commute with σ_i. For j<i, split x_j=Aσ_i^{−1}Kσ_iB and use the mixed braid relation to derive σ_iAσ_i^{−1}=Aσ_i^{−1}σ_{i+1}; commute σ_{i+1} past K, write B=σ_{i+1}B′, then use σ_{i+1}σ_iσ_{i+1}=σ_iσ_{i+1}σ_i and commute σ_i past B′. This gives σ_ix_j=x_jσ_i, including the intervening σ_{i+1} factor. For j=i+1, set C=σ_{n−1}^{−1}⋯σ_{i+2}^{−1} and D=C^{-1}; direct expansion gives σ_i^{−1}x_{i+1}σ_i=Cσ_{i+1}σ_i²σ_{i+1}^{−1}D=x_{i+1}x_ix_{i+1}^{−1}. For j=i the mixed braid relation gives σ_i^{−1}x_iσ_i=x_{i+1}. Invert these conjugation identities to obtain the second table. Each relation is a word consequence of the two Artin families; the published geometric relation items transfer them to G_n.

items.title: Every trivial braid word combs as W_1W_2
items.statement: Assume n≥2 and let W be a word in σ_1^{±1},…,σ_{n−1}^{±1} whose geometric image is the trivial braid. Then W is equivalent, using only the two Artin relations and free insertions and deletions of σ^{±1}σ^{∓1} pairs, to a product W_1W_2 in which W_1 is a word in x_1^{±1},…,x_{n−1}^{±1} and W_2 is a word in σ_1^{±1},…,σ_{n−2}^{±1}.
items.proof_strategy: Rewrite W by the prefix-insertion lemma as the product of its combing factors. Reduce each factor by the six cases: factors reducing to the empty word are deleted, factors reducing to x-letters are kept, and factors reducing to σ_1,…,σ_{n−2} letters are kept as lower-rank letters. The result is a word in the x-letters and the lower-rank σ-letters. Now collect: repeatedly take the leftmost σ-letter that has an x-letter to its left and move the x-letter one step left using the conjugation table of the lower-rank lemma; at every step the x-letter is replaced by a product of x-letters and their inverses, so the x-letters stay within the alphabet x_1,…,x_{n−1} and the σ-letter moves one position right. Each move decreases the total number of (x-letter, σ-letter) inversions, so the process terminates at a product W_1W_2 with all x-letters in W_1 and all lower-rank letters in W_2. This is the collection step of the source's proof; no geometric input beyond the triviality of φ(W) is used.

items.title: The combed geometric decomposition is unique
items.statement: Assume AC and n≥2. Let φ:B_n→G_n be the published Artin-to-geometric surjection, and let W₁ be a word in x_1^{±1},…,x_{n−1}^{±1} and W₂ a word in σ_1^{±1},…,σ_{n−2}^{±1} with φ(W₁W₂)=1. Write A_{ij}∈G_n for the geometric standard pure generators and Ã_{ij}∈B_n for their Artin-word lifts σ_{j−1}⋯σ_{i+1}σ_i²σ_{i+1}^{−1}⋯σ_{j−1}^{−1}, so φ(Ã_{ij})=A_{ij}. Put P_i=A_{i+1,n}⋯A_{n−1,n}∈G_n and P̃_i=Ã_{i+1,n}⋯Ã_{n−1,n}∈B_n. Then (i) each φ(x_i) is pure and φ(x_i)=P_i^{-1}A_{in}P_i, where P_i uses only standard generators A_{jn} with j>i; at the word level, x_i≡P̃_i^{-1}Ã_{in}P̃_i; the elements Ψ_n(φ(x_1)),…,Ψ_n(φ(x_{n−1})) form a free basis of the free kernel of PB_n→PB_{n−1}; (ii) φ(W₁)=1 and W₁ freely reduces in the x-letters to the empty word, with each inverse x-pair expanding to permitted free cancellations of σ-pairs; and (iii) φ(W₂)=1 and, viewing the same letter word as an element of B_{n−1}, its geometric image under the rank-(n−1) surjection φ_{n−1}:B_{n−1}→G_{n−1} is trivial, so φ_{n−1}(W₂)=1∈G_{n−1}. This asserts triviality of the geometric image, not W₂=1 in B_{n−1}.
items.proof_strategy: First prove x_i≡P̃_i^{-1}Ã_{in}P̃_i by an explicit free-cancellation induction on products of the Artin lifts Ã_{jn}; applying φ gives the correctly typed geometric conjugation by P_i. Under AC, the batch-21 forgetful sequence identifies the free kernel K with the basis Ψ_n(A_{jn}). The lower-rank inclusion is realized explicitly: the safe embedding E maps the (n−1)-disk into a subdisk tangent at q_n, agrees with the center dilation A on all lower basepoints and half-twist supports, and avoids q_n. The radial interpolation E_t consists of embeddings; its moving-basepoint homotopy shows E_* on ordered configuration π₁ is injective. Thus the straight-strand extension has image meeting K only in 1. The conjugates t_i=w_i^{-1}a_iw_i, with w_i=a_{i+1}⋯a_{n−1}, generate F(a_1,…,a_{n−1}); a descending endomorphism θ(a_i)=θ(w_i)a_iθ(w_i)^{-1} is a left inverse to a_i↦t_i, proving they freely form a basis. For the decomposition, W₂ is in the stabilized lower-rank image; endpoint permutations show its lower braid is pure, the trivial intersection forces both components to be trivial, and freeness gives the x-word cancellations. In the radial embedding route, compare configuration loops by dropping the last coordinate; the inner punctured disks retract radially to their boundary meridians and the outer collar retracts to the outer boundary.

items.title: The Artin presentation is complete for geometric braids
items.statement: Assume AC. For every n≥1 the published surjection φ_n:B_n^{Artin}→B_n^{geom} of [[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]] is an isomorphism. Equivalently, every word in σ_1^{±1},…,σ_{n−1}^{±1} whose geometric braid is trivial is equivalent to the empty word using only the two Artin relations and free insertions and deletions, so the Artin presentation is a presentation of the geometric braid group.
items.proof_strategy: Induct on n≥1. Base n=1: B_1^{Artin} has no generators, so the only word is empty. Step n≥2: let W be an Artin word with φ(W)=1. Comb it as W≡W_1W_2 using the combing lemma, with W_1 in the x-letters and W_2 in σ_1,…,σ_{n−2}. The uniqueness lemma gives φ(W_1)=1 with W_1 freely trivial, hence W_1 reduces to the empty word by permitted moves; and it gives that W_2 read on n−1 strands is the trivial braid of rank n−1, so by the induction hypothesis applied to the rank n−1 presentation, W_2 is equivalent to the empty word by relations among σ_1,…,σ_{n−2}, which are relators of B_n^{Artin}. Hence W≡1. Surjectivity of φ_n is the published proposition, so φ_n is an isomorphism. Check the base-case input explicitly: at n=2 the kernel of PB_2→PB_1 is PB_2 itself, freely generated by the single element A_{12}=σ_1² by the batch-21 free-kernel lemma, so the uniqueness step has content; no injectivity of any Artin presentation is assumed anywhere in the induction.

items.title: All four classical braid models realize the Artin presentation
items.statement: Assume AC and n≥1. The four models — the Artin-presentation group B_n^{Artin}, the geometric braid group B_n^{geom} on Q_n, the fundamental group of the unordered configuration space C_n(int D²) (the published configuration braid group), and the boundary-fixed punctured-disk mapping class group Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²) — are connected by the canonical isomorphisms φ_n, the published configuration isomorphism and the AC-dependent boundary-fixed mapping-class isomorphism of [[thm-braid-group-is-the-boundary-fixed-mapping-class-group-of-the-punctured-disk]] (an in-run batch-20 scaffold, not a published supplier), and under these identifications the Artin generator σ_i corresponds to the elementary geometric half twist, to the monodromy loop of the adjacent transposition (i,i+1), and to the half twist supported near the i-th and (i+1)-st punctures. Consequently each of the four models carries the Artin presentation with these corresponding generators.
items.proof_strategy: Compose the maps: the completeness theorem gives φ_n:B_n^{Artin}→B_n^{geom} an isomorphism; the published canonical isomorphism identifies B_n^{geom} with the fundamental group of the unordered configuration space at the fixed base configuration through the inverse-slice map; the AC-dependent boundary-fixed mapping-class isomorphism of the batch-20 in-run scaffold [[thm-braid-group-is-the-boundary-fixed-mapping-class-group-of-the-punctured-disk]] identifies B_n^{geom} with Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²), sending the standard geometric half twist to its disk-supported class. Track the generators through the composites: σ_i↦the elementary half twist by definition of φ_n; the configuration isomorphism carries that half twist to the loop with monodromy the adjacent transposition by the published endpoint-permutation identity; the mapping-class isomorphism carries it to the disk-supported half twist. Each composite is an isomorphism of the same two groups at a common basepoint, so all six comparison maps are canonical and the generator correspondences agree; AC is inherited from the mapping-class supplier and the completeness theorem. The mapping-class supplier is a ready in-run batch-20 scaffold, not a published theorem, and its authored proof is owed the Step-3 convention check recorded in the batch-22 cross-batch input.

title: Artin Presentation Completeness and Braid Combing — Examples

items.title: Combing a four-strand braid word
items.statement: In B_4 consider W=σ_3σ_2σ_3σ_2^{−1}σ_3^{−1}σ_2^{−1}σ_1σ_2σ_1σ_2^{−1}σ_1^{−1}σ_2^{−1}. Its first six letters cancel by one three-strand relation and the last six letters are σ_1σ_2σ_1σ_2^{−1}σ_1^{−1}σ_2^{−1}, itself trivial in B_3 by one three-strand relation, so W traces the trivial braid. Tracking the last point gives the position sequence 4,3,2,2,3,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4; prefix insertion writes W as a product of twelve combing factors, and the six-case reduction reduces them, in order, to x_3, x_2, σ_2, x_2^{−1}, x_3^{−1}, σ_2^{−1}, σ_1, σ_2, σ_1, σ_2^{−1}, σ_1^{−1}, σ_2^{−1}. Collecting the x-letters to the left gives W≡W_1W_2 with W_1=x_3x_2x_2^{−1}x_3^{−1}x_2x_2^{−1}, which freely reduces to the empty word, and W_2=σ_1σ_2σ_1σ_2^{−1}σ_1^{−1}σ_2^{−1}, which is trivial in B_3 by one three-strand relation.
items.proof_strategy: Verify triviality first: σ_3σ_2σ_3≡σ_2σ_3σ_2 makes the first six letters σ_2σ_3(σ_2σ_2^{−1})σ_3^{−1}σ_2^{−1} reduce to the empty word, and σ_1σ_2σ_1≡σ_2σ_1σ_2 makes the last six letters σ_2σ_1(σ_2σ_2^{−1})σ_1^{−1}σ_2^{−1} reduce to the empty word, each by one three-strand relation and two σ-pair deletions. Track the point that starts at position 4 through the twelve letters with the interchange rule to obtain the displayed position sequence. Apply prefix insertion with those positions to build the twelve factors; reduce each with the six cases: factors 1 and 2 are of the x_k case, factors 4 and 5 are of the x_k^{−1} case, factors 3 and 6 are of the lower-rank cases (σ_2 and σ_2^{−1} respectively), and factors 7–12 are of the commuting lower-rank case, leaving the displayed letters. Collect with the conjugation table: moving x_2^{−1} and x_3^{−1} left past σ_2, σ_2^{−1} cancels the surviving σ-pair and produces only x-letters, so W≡W_1W_2 with the displayed W_1 and W_2. Finally W_1 is freely trivial by two cancellations of x-pairs, and W_2 is trivial in B_3 by one three-strand relation; display the full reduction table. The example claims no uniqueness statement and uses the geometric validity of the three-strand relation.

items.title: The free-kernel words for three-strand braid combing
items.statement: Assume AC for the free-kernel basis. For n=3 the combing words of [[def-zariski-braid-combing-words-alpha-and-x]] are x_2=σ_2² and x_1=σ_2^{−1}σ_1²σ_2. With the standard pure braids A_{23}=σ_2² and A_{13}=σ_2σ_1²σ_2^{−1} of [[def-standard-pure-braid-generators]], free cancellation gives x_2=A_{23} and x_1=A_{23}^{−1}A_{13}A_{23}, which is the combing identity of [[lem-the-combed-geometric-decomposition-is-unique]] at n=3. Hence the free kernel of PB_3→PB_2, freely generated by A_{13},A_{23} through the batch-21 identification, is equally freely generated by x_1,x_2, matching the two clockwise based meridian classes of the twice-punctured disk fiber of the forgetting map (the inverses of the positively oriented meridian classes).
items.proof_strategy: Expand the definitions: α_3=1 and α_2=σ_2, so x_2=α_3^{−1}σ_2²α_3=σ_2² and x_1=α_2^{−1}σ_1²α_2=σ_2^{−1}σ_1²σ_2. Then check the two displayed identities by free cancellation: A_{23}^{−1}A_{13}A_{23}=σ_2^{−2}·σ_2σ_1²σ_2^{−1}·σ_2² reduces to σ_2^{−1}σ_1²σ_2=x_1, while A_{23}=σ_2²=x_2. The free-basis conclusion is the n=3 instance of the preceding lemma, which supplies the conjugating identity and the basis statement through the batch-21 free-kernel lemma; no relation beyond free cancellation and no later Garside, center or faithfulness result is consumed. The two displayed free-cancellation computations are themselves choice-free; the final free-basis conclusion inherits the AC hypothesis of the preceding lemma, so the item states AC for that basis and declares the published axiom-of-choice definition together with the AC⇒DC theorem.

items.title: Visible Artin relations alone do not prove presentation completeness
items.statement: Assume AC. The inference 'the relations of a presentation hold in a group G and the images of its generators generate G, hence the presentation presents G' is invalid. For the presented group P=⟨x | x⁴=1⟩ and G=⟨g | g²=1⟩, the assignment x↦g kills the defining relator because g⁴=1 and g generates G, so it induces a surjection P→G; but it is not injective, since x² maps to 1 while x²≠1 in P. Consequently the published verification that the Artin relations hold among the geometric half twists and that the σ_i generate the geometric braid group — which yields only the surjection φ — cannot by itself prove that the Artin presentation presents the geometric braid group; the missing obligation is exactly the triviality of ker φ, supplied by the combing kernel argument of [[thm-the-artin-presentation-is-complete-for-geometric-braids]].
items.proof_strategy: Use von Dyck twice. First, x↦[1]_2 defines a homomorphism φ:P→ℤ/2 because x⁴ maps to [4]_2=[0]_2; its image contains [1]_2, so φ is surjective. Second, x↦[1]_4 defines ψ:P→ℤ/4 because x⁴ maps to [4]_4=[0]_4; ψ(x²)=[2]_4≠[0]_4 by the standard representatives, so x²≠1 in P. Hence x² is a nontrivial element of kerφ and φ is a non-injective surjection, refuting the inference. The braid application: verifying that the Artin relations hold among the geometric half twists and that the σ_i generate the geometric braid group is exactly a von Dyck construction of the surjection φ, so it too yields only surjectivity; the triviality of kerφ needs the separate combing argument. AC is carried because the item consumes the AC-dependent completeness theorem as its supplier; the counterexample's own computation is choice-free.
